red.purpose: The checker's pen as line work: clouds, deltas, strikes, leaders, link underlines, the running column, progress, focus.

red-ink.purpose: Red as letters: the hand face, initials, delta letters, Withdrawn and Incident stamps (about 5.5:1 on film).

amber-ink.purpose: Not yet: Preliminary, Draft, Not for issue, Hold.

amber-wash.purpose: The only tint fill: behind Hold and On hold stamps. Base amber #e2a62b at 24%.

guide.purpose: 1px lettering guides under headings only; never text, fill or border.

film.purpose: The ground of every sheet and the fill of every drawn part.

ink.purpose: All lettering, the frame, outlines, ticks and list dashes.

ink-soft.purpose: Label lettering, captions, signature lines, struck text, empty register rows.

rule.purpose: Row rules inside tables and schedules: graphite at 25%.

display.purpose: The cover title (88px) and the single heading of each closing sheet (64 to 104px), lettered on cap and baseline guides.

headline.purpose: One per sheet, balanced, on a 1px non-photo-blue baseline guide.

title.purpose: Names inside drawn parts: reviewer desks, schedule row heads, regret-card heads.

note.purpose: The one note at the foot of a content sheet, after a NOTE label.

body.purpose: Sentences on the sheet and list items.

body-sm.purpose: Table cells, schedule entries and definitions (22 to 24px).

caption.purpose: One-line supporting text under a bold name, in Graphite Soft (20 to 21px). Never a paragraph.

part-title.purpose: Uppercase title strip of a drawn part; checklist responses.

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels, column heads, title-block cells, the NOTE marker, illustrative-data labels, in Graphite Soft. The type floor.

block-entry.purpose: The Rev letter in the title block; the sheet number sets at 700.

stamp.purpose: Uppercase rubber stamps, tilted, in a stamp ink.

stamp-sm.purpose: Register status and scenario stamps; 18px inside schedule cells.

hand.purpose: The checker's red pen only: notes, initials, the asterisk (22 to 34px).

code.purpose: File names, paths and commands only; 20 to 22px in chips, titles and tables.

shadows.name: stamp-double-ring
shadows.purpose: Inner ring of a rubber stamp inside its 3.5px border (2px and 3px on small stamps). Zero blur: line work.

shadows.name: running-column-underbar
shadows.purpose: Marks the issue-schedule column now in progress.

shadows.name: control-shade-line
shadows.purpose: Heavier drafting line along a control's bottom edge; Redline on Approve.

motion.name: settle-budget
motion.purpose: Every effect is finite, plays only on the live audience sheet (section.co-live) inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, uses backwards fills, and has finished by 4.95s.

motion.name: ink
motion.value: clip-path wipe left to right, 420-900ms ease-out; cover title cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
motion.purpose: Lettering, notes, definitions and initials ink in.

motion.name: trace
motion.purpose: A revision cloud is drawn around its box.

motion.name: stamp
motion.value: scale 1.5 to 0.95 to 1 at the stamp's tilt, 300-320ms ease-out
motion.purpose: A rubber stamp lands with a press.

motion.name: strike
motion.value: scaleX 0 to 1 from the left, 300ms ease-out

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Delta tags and checker's ticks appear.

motion.name: fade-rise
motion.purpose: Rows, list items and notes arrive in order.

motion.name: develop
motion.value: grayscale(1) contrast(0.7) brightness(1.25) to none, 1600ms ease-out
motion.purpose: The bio portrait develops on the film.

motion.name: token
motion.purpose: The AI-0142 token travels the review loop and back until clean.

motion.name: nudge
motion.value: translateY(-3px) with a 5px Redline shade line, 900ms ease-in-out, 2 iterations
motion.purpose: The Approve control asks for a decision.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: The only loop: the running-cell dot while a presenter-started schedule runs.

motion.name: transition-sheet
motion.value: 650ms; incoming translateX(56px) and fade, outgoing translateX(-28px) and fade
motion.purpose: Default: the next sheet is laid on the set.

motion.name: transition-handoff
motion.value: 900ms cross-fade; outgoing gone by 40%, incoming from 55%; view-transition-name co-hero
motion.purpose: Lets the change tag morph from sheet to sheet.

narrative.overview:
Every AI-written change is a drawing revision: clouded where it changed, and not issued until someone checks and approves it. The deck is a drawing set on drafting film. Each slide is a sheet with a drawn frame and zone references, a title block that numbers it, and graphite lettering set on non-photo-blue guide lines. Change is marked the way a checker marks a drawing, with red revision clouds, delta tags, strike-throughs and initials, and status is applied with rubber stamps.

Density is a working drawing, not a poster. A sheet carries one lettered statement, one drawn part (a register, a schedule, a spec sheet, a checklist) and one note. Caps labels letter the parts at 18px; anything read as a sentence stays large enough for the back of a conference room. Graphite carries the content, and color always means something: red for change and decision, stamp inks for status. The world refuses the neon AI-talk deck, the white corporate template, and borrowed aviation.

Motion draws the sheet while the audience watches, then holds still: lettering inks in from the left, clouds trace around their box, stamps land with a press, and the checker's initials go on last. The authored markup is always the finished drawing.
keyCharacteristics: Flat graphite ink on pale drafting film; no cast shadows and no glow.
A drawn sheet frame with zone references, and a title block (Checked, Approved, Rev, Sheet) on every interior sheet.
One condensed engineering face for all lettering, a felt-pen hand only for the checker, and a mono only for files and commands.
Red is the checker's pen: clouds, deltas, strikes, initials, withdrawals.
Rubber stamps in amber (not yet), green (issued) and red (withdrawn).
Finite motion on the live audience sheet only; every static view is complete.

rules.name: The Static Sheet Rule
rules.body: The authored markup is the finished drawing; motion only reveals it. Effects play once on the live audience sheet (`section.co-live`), fill backwards, and settle within 4.95s. Print, reduced-motion, presenter and no-script views show the same complete sheet. The one infinite motion is the active-cell pulse while a presenter-started schedule runs.

rules.name: The Honest Sheet Rule
rules.body: Simulated data is labeled on the sheet itself, in label lettering ("Illustrative: ...", "Fictional changes, illustrative only"), never only in speaker notes.

rules.name: The Redline Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what changed, what was decided, and where attention goes next (the running stage, the focus ring, a link's underline). It never fills a surface and never sets headings or prose.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Red strokes use Redline; red letters use Redline Ink, which holds about 5.5:1 on film where Redline holds about 4.2:1.

rules.name: The Stamp Ink Rule
rules.body: Each stamp ink has one meaning: amber is not yet, green is issued, red is withdrawn, void or incident. Stamp inks color stamps and the schedule's outcome marks, and nothing else.

rules.name: The Three Pens Rule
rules.body: Saira letters everything typeset. The hand face is only the checker's red pen: markup, initials, the asterisk on a weakened test. The mono face is only file names, paths and commands. If a line is neither the checker's markup nor a literal path or command, it is Saira.

rules.name: The Lettering Guide Rule
rules.body: Headings sit on non-photo-blue guides, the way a drafter letters a sheet. A headline gets one 1px guide at its baseline (41px down a 54px line); a display heading gets a cap guide and a baseline guide. Guides start 10px before the first letter and run 26px past the last.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: At 1280x720, label lettering is never below 18px and anything read as a sentence is never below 22px; one-line captions may sit at 20 to 21px. The change tag's cell captions (16px), its small delta, and the schedule's outcome stamps (17px) sit below the floor inside compact drawn parts. They are known exceptions, not precedents.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Nothing crosses the frame line. The 28px margin holds only zone ticks and references; photos, tables and stamps stay inside the frame and clear of the title block.

rules.name: The Title Block Rule
rules.body: Every interior sheet carries the title block. Its signatures start as blank dotted lines, and only the sheet's state fills them: checked, approved, and revision A, B or C (`checked`, `approved`, `rev-a/b/c`). A sheet that has not earned a signature shows the empty line.

rules.name: The One Note Rule
rules.body: A content sheet ends with one note at most: a NOTE label and one line in Note lettering, 16px above the title block. Reference sheets may put a plain 22px source line in the same place instead.

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: No blur and no glow. A box-shadow with a blur radius is not part of this world; zero-blur rings, underbars and shade lines are line work and belong.

rules.name: The Drawn Cloud Rule
rules.body: A revision cloud is always a drawn asset, never a CSS border, radius or dash pattern. Masks never load from asset files, because Chrome drops them from PDF export; inline data-URI and gradient masks are fine.

rules.name: The Hand-Placed Lean Rule
rules.body: Only what a person applies by hand is rotated: stamps, initials, strike-throughs. Typeset lettering, frames and drawn parts stay square.

rules.name: The Two Ticks Rule
rules.body: A graphite tick is recorded evidence; a red tick in a box is the checker's. Never swap them.

dos: **Do** letter each sheet's headline at 48px on a 54px line with its 1px non-photo-blue baseline guide.
**Do** cloud exactly what changed with a drawn cloud asset, and tag it with the delta letter that matches the revision table.
**Do** fill title-block signatures only from the sheet's state (`checked`, `approved`, `rev-a/b/c`), and leave the dotted line empty until the sheet earns it.
**Do** end a content sheet with one note, 16px above the title block.
**Do** label simulated data on the sheet itself, in Label lettering.
**Do** build new drawn parts from film fill, a 2.5px graphite outline, 1.5px dividers and 1px Hairline Rule rows.
**Do** author the static sheet first: anything the runtime changes gets a static twin that prints (`co-static`) and a live twin shown only in the audience window (`co-dynamic`).
**Do** gate motion to the live audience sheet (`section.co-live`) inside a no-preference reduced-motion query, with backwards fills, finished by 4.95s.
donts: **Don't** use red for anything that did not change, was not decided, and is not the next point of attention: no red headings, red emphasis or decorative red rules.
**Don't** set any text in non-photo blue, or draw it heavier than 1px.
**Don't** set prose in the hand face, or anything but file names, paths and commands in the mono.
**Don't** fake a revision cloud with a CSS border, radius or dash pattern, or load a mask from an asset file.
**Don't** rotate typeset lettering, frames or drawn parts; only stamps, initials and strikes lean.
**Don't** add looping motion; the only loop is the running-cell pulse while a presenter-started schedule runs.
**Don't** put content in the 28px zone margin or over the title block.
**Don't** drift toward the neon AI-talk deck, a white corporate template, or borrowed aviation.
**Don't** letter below the floor (18px labels, 22px sentences) to fit content onto a sheet.
**Don't** reach for the template's layout classes (`lead`, `invert`, `columns3`) when a drawn part fits; they stay only for template compatibility.
